Article Title: India aims to raise share in global space economy to 8-9%: Former Isro chief S Somanath

NEW DELHI: Former Isro chairman S Somanath on Tuesday said India is aiming to increase its share in the global space economy to 8-9%, highlighting the need for stronger collaboration between the government and private sector to achieve the target.Speaking to reporters, Somanath said India's contribution to the global space economy was around 2% in 2020, when the sector was estimated to be worth approximately $550 billion. India's share at the time stood at around $8-9 billion, he said.“Now we are aspiring to reach something like 8-9% of the global space economy in every segment,” Somanath said.“Real scale in economic activity will happen only if the government and the private sector work together in terms of investment, revenue generation, businesses, and global markets,” he added.Pointing to the growing importance of commercial space activities, the former Isro chief said services and delivery account for around 60% of the global space economy.“Around 60% of the global space economy comes from services and delivery, and in that segment we need to slowly show our presence,” he said.Somanath also underlined that the space sector was globally interconnected, with technological developments and economic activities in one country influencing the wider international ecosystem.Referring to the space sector reforms announced in 2020, he said India's growing participation in the global space economy was also influencing how space activities were being undertaken in other countries.

India slammed Turkey at the United Nations for its "blatant and intentional" decision to exclude New Delhi and other member states from consultations on a resolution on cooperation between the UN and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).India voted against the draft resolution, which was adopted by the UN General Assembly with 112 votes in favour, six against and 39 abstentions. Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Israel and the US also voted against it. Iraq introduced the resolution, while Turkey served as its facilitator.India's deputy permanent representative to the UN Yojna Patel said the OIC's Permanent Observer Mission chose to exclude the Indian delegation and a number of other countries while circulating successive drafts of the resolution.While delivering India's explanation of vote, Patel also called for an investigation into the working methods adopted by the resolution's facilitator."My delegation has voted against this resolution not only because of its substantive aspects, but also for an even more concerning matter regarding the working methods adopted by the facilitator who convened negotiations on the same," Patel said."This is not only shocking but also sets a bad precedent of delegations excluding specific member states to enable their agendas," she added.Patel also said that despite some delegations registering their objections in subsequent rounds, the "facilitators still chose to not include select countries". Other basic procedures, such as acknowledging inputs, were also "blatantly disregarded", indicating that the exclusion was by design rather than by mistake.She said it was "unfortunate that there are member states who publicly profess commitment to multilateralism and completely turn a blind eye to its core guiding principles".Underlining that the UN was founded on the principles of sovereign equality, inclusivity and multilateral cooperation, Patel said differences of position among member states were inherent to multilateral diplomacy and "cannot, in themselves, justify blatant and intentional exclusion from the consultations on matters before the General Assembly"."My delegation strongly objects to such working methods that try to hoodwink excluded delegations into believing that this was just a technical update, which it was not," she said.In a thinly veiled reference to Pakistan , India also voiced regret that the OIC had "once again allowed itself to be systematically misused by one member state to weaponise OIC resolutions and declarations against India through false and baseless allegations".Pakistan is a founding and prominent member of the 57-member OIC.Greece and Cyprus also raised "serious concerns" regarding the conduct of negotiations under Turkiye's facilitation."Throughout the process, the European Union submitted comments and amendments in good faith, which were neither meaningfully addressed nor accompanied by substantial explanations for their rejection. Furthermore, revised drafts were circulated without adequate consultation," Greece's delegate said.
Article Summary: India voted against the draft resolution, which was adopted by the UN General Assembly with 112 votes in favour, six against and 39 abstentions. Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Israel and the US also voted against it. Iraq introduced the resolution, while Turkey served as its facilitator.

Article Title: Amid China rivalry, India joins move to shield AI tech chain

NEW DELHI: India has joined United States and eight other Pax Silica initiative partners in signing the San Francisco Declaration to jointly protect critical infrastructure and supply chains essential for artificial intelligence (AI).The declaration is an international agreement that is being seen as an attempt to protect the full technology chain needed to build AI - from essential raw materials to manufacturing and energy networks.Amid intensifying rivalry with China, the agreement reinforces the importance of coordinated efforts to address economic coercion, supply chain disruptions, and non-market policies and practices and their market-distorting effects, while protecting private investment and ensuring a level playing field for innovation and growth.It treats the hardware, digital systems and logistics powering AI as vital national assets that partner countries must protect together for "economic security and enduring prosperity".Pax Silica is State Department's flagship effort on AI, renamed Super Intelligence or SI by President Donald Trump, and supply chain security, advancing new economic security consensus among allies and trusted partners."We affirm that the safeguarding of these sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure is a shared endeavour; that the security of each participant is strengthened by the vigilance of all; and that we engage in this common cause as aligned partners - in defense of prosperity and independence of our peoples," said the declaration.India joined US-led Pax Silica initiative in Feb this year, as both sides hailed a growing geopolitical consensus that "economic security is national security, and national security is economic security".State Department had then said India brings to Pax Silica a deep talent pool, processing and refining capacity for critical minerals, investments in AI infrastructure and an understanding of the importance of trusted technologies.The declaration was signed at a meeting of the founders of Pax Silica initiative convened by US Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg Sunday. It was released by govts of US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, UAE and UK.

Article Title: Parents fled Mozambique with unregistered newborn; 26 yrs later, Gujarat woman gets Indian passport
Article Text:
Dolly Vadalia, brought to India from Mozambique as a newborn, received her passport after a 26-year citizenship battle

NEW DELHI: A 26-year-old woman from Gujarat, whose Indian parents brought her to the country as an unregistered newborn while fleeing floods in Mozambique, has finally received an Indian passport after a prolonged citizenship battle. Dolly Vadalia received the passport on November 11, following a Union home ministry memorandum recognising her as an Indian citizen, news agency PTI reported citing her brother-in-law Ronak Vadalia on Monday.Born on February 18, 2000, in Xai-Xai, Mozambique, Dolly was just 18 to 20 days old when her parents evacuated her from the country after a tropical cyclone triggered massive floods. The family returned to India and settled in Rajkot, their hometown.Dolly's citizenship status became a hurdle after she married Khilankumar Vadalia, a Rajkot resident employed in Canada, in 2023. Her inability to obtain an Indian passport kept the couple separated.Her three passport applications, filed in 2023 and 2025, were rejected because she could not establish her Indian citizenship through the required documents. Authorities sought proof of cancellation of her emergency certificate or consular registration of her birth.The matter was subsequently taken up with Lok Sabha MPs Ramesh Dhaduk and Parshottam Rupala, who forwarded it to the Rajkot collectorate, the Gandhinagar secretariat, the MHA and the MEA, Ronak said as cited by PTI.The MEA sought the MHA's opinion. In October last year, the home ministry reiterated that under Section 4(1)(b) of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a child born outside India must have their birth registered at an Indian consulate within one year to claim citizenship by descent. Although Dolly had an Aadhaar card, it was not sufficient to establish her eligibility for an Indian passport, Ronak said.On April 30 this year, a single-judge bench of the Gujarat high court observed that Dolly's parents had not followed the mandatory birth registration procedure. It held that she was neither an Indian citizen by birth nor by descent under Sections 3 and 4 of the Act."The court advised us to apply for citizenship; however, we could not file an application initially because we lacked a valid passport — a mandatory requirement for the process," Ronak said, explaining why the family subsequently approached a division bench.Following a background check and verification, the Indian embassy in Mozambique and the MHA issued a memorandum."Based on this, Dolly's birth was registered with the Indian High Commission in Maputo, Mozambique, in November. Using that certificate, we applied for a passport, which we finally received last week," he said.
Article Summary: Dolly Vadalia received the passport on November 11, following a Union home ministry memorandum recognising her as an Indian citizen. Born on February 18, 2000, in Xai-Xai, Mozambique, her parents evacuated her from the country after a tropical cyclone triggered massive floods. Her inability to obtain an Indian passport kept the couple separated.

Article Title: '520 drains discharge wastewater in the Yamuna': SC raps admin over rising pollution despite huge spending
Article Text:
SC says Yamuna pollution has worsened despite heavy spending and directs CPCB to monitor water quality across state and district boundaries

Authorities to face penalties for worsening water quality

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday pulled up civic authorities and Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) over the worsening pollution in the Yamuna despite large sums being spent on cleaning the river. The bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan directed CPCB to monitor water quality where the river and 520 drains enter and exit states, Union territories and districts.It also said authorities would be held accountable if water quality deteriorates in their jurisdiction, news agency PTI reported citing an order dated November 4. The matter has been listed for further hearing on January 13."This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna. This is why, despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, pollution in the Yamuna has only increased," the bench saidThe court said industrial pollutants and untreated sewage must be stopped at the source. It observed that building more sewage treatment plants alone would not be enough to address the problem.The bench said sewage should first be tapped and then treated wherever pollution cannot be prevented at the source. However, it flagged the difficulty of doing so because of weak sewage networks and the mixing of stormwater and sewage drains."Where that is not possible, the sewage must first be tapped and then treated.However, tapping will remain a challenge in absence of a robust sewage system and due to joining of stormwater and sewage drains. This court is further of the opinion that it would be difficult, if not impossible, for civic authorities to tap sewage in most illegal and unauthorised colonies built on encroached land, since they have not been built on a grid layout and have hardly any space for laying a sewage system," it said.The Supreme Court directed the CPCB to track water quality at the entry and exit points of states, Union territories and districts. If the water deteriorates on any parameter while passing through a jurisdiction, the concerned administration will be held accountable and penalised."If the water quality deteriorates on any parameter while flowing through, or exiting a state/Union territory or a district therein, that state/Union territory or district... shall be held accountable and penalised. The said compensation/ fine shall be deposited with the registry of this court," the bench said.The court asked the CPCB to propose a formula for calculating the compensation or fine.It also directed the board to investigate incidents indicating pollution in the river, including fish deaths, white foam on the surface, eutrophication or algal blooms, and spikes in biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD) or total suspended solids (TSS).The CPCB's reports must identify the causes of such incidents or increases in pollution levels and recommend remedial measures, the court said.The bench further directed central and state ministries, departments and agencies to provide the CPCB and its experts with administrative, technical, logistical and operational support.Public and private entities involved in wastewater, solid waste and effluent treatment have also been asked to provide CPCB officials and designated third-party agencies unrestricted access to their premises, installations and records. This includes access for surprise inspections, sample collection, audits and checks of monitoring equipment.The court said plant operators and concerned authorities must also provide complete data access and cooperate with the integration of their systems into the CPCB's centralised monitoring network.
Article Summary: Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan directed CPCB to monitor water quality where the river and 520 drains enter and exit states, Union territories and districts. It said authorities would be held accountable if water quality deteriorates in their jurisdiction. The matter has been listed for further hearing on January 13.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh 's Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa on Tuesday said that the Election Commission 's database does not contain information regarding religion or caste.During a press conference, Rinwa said it was impossible for the poll panel to conduct any analysis based on religion and caste using the electoral rolls."If you look at our electoral rolls or our database, they contain the following details for each voter: their name, the type of relationship, the name of the relative, their age or date of birth, house number, and gender," the UP CEO said."Our database does not contain information regarding religion, caste, or any other such details; therefore, it is impossible for us to conduct any analysis based on these factors using our electoral rolls," he added."We do not possess any data based on religion. Approximately 2 crore 58 lakh citizens living in Uttar Pradesh are currently not included in the voter list," he further said.This clarification comes days after Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath claimed that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing from the state's electoral rolls after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).Adityanath said the Muslim voter population had increased by 1.65 per cent after the revision, while raising concerns over the deletion of Hindu voters' names."That is why we also submitted our memorandum to the Election Commission. Cyclonic Storm Akvan, currently positioned over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19 before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Tuesday.According to the IMD's national bulletin issued at 2:30 am IST on November 17, the storm remained nearly stationary over the previous nine hours and continued to be centred over the same region.The weather system was located near latitude 12.2°N and longitude 85.7°E, around 610 km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha, according to the news agency ANI.The IMD said the storm is likely to move north-northwestwards and strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the evening of November 17.It is subsequently expected to continue moving northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19.According to the forecast, the system will continue its northwestward movement before crossing the Andhra Pradesh and yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20.At the time of landfall, the cyclone is expected to generate maximum sustained wind speeds of 120-130 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 145 kmph, the bulletin stated.The IMD has issued an orange alert for the Andhra Pradesh coast and adjoining coastal areas of south Odisha, warning of the potential impact of the approaching cyclone.The weather department has forecast light to moderate rainfall at places on November 18 and 19, potentially causing waterlogging in parts of Tamil Nadu.For coastal Andhra Pradesh, the IMD has predicted light to moderate rainfall at several locations, accompanied by heavy showers at isolated places on November 18.The situation could intensify on November 19 and 20, with isolated areas of north coastal Andhra Pradesh likely to receive extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 21 cm.In Odisha, isolated areas are likely to experience heavy rainfall on November 18, with light to moderate showers expected at some places.The IMD has further forecast light to moderate rainfall across most places in the state, along with heavy to very heavy showers at isolated locations between November 19 and 21.The weather department's latest warning indicates that the approaching cyclone could bring intense rainfall and strong winds to several coastal districts, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and adjoining regions.
Article Summary: Cyclonic Storm Akvan is currently positioned over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. Article Title: NMC asks all government medical colleges, attached hospitals to join road accident cashless treatment scheme
Article Text:
NMC has asked deans, directors, principals and medical superintendents to accord priority to the exercise and take necessary steps to facilitate their institutions’ participation.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has directed all government medical colleges and their attached hospitals across the country to onboard the Centre’s PM-RAHAT scheme, aimed at ensuring cashless treatment for road accident victims during the critical golden hour.In a public notice issued on Monday, the NMC has asked deans, directors, principals and medical superintendents to accord priority to the exercise and take necessary steps to facilitate their institutions’ participation. The move follows a request from the Union Health Ministry’s Trauma and Burn Cell to the commission on October 28 to widen the network of hospitals under the scheme.The PM-RAHAT (Prime Minister’s Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment) scheme provides cashless treatment of up to Rs 1.5 lakh per accident victim for a maximum of seven days from the date of the accident at designated hospitals. Non-designated hospitals can provide stabilisation treatment to victims, ensuring that emergency care is not delayed while patients are referred to higher-level facilities.The guidelines issued by the National Health Authority (NHA) provide for two categories of hospitals under the scheme: designated hospitals, which can provide stabilisation, trauma and polytrauma services, and PM-RAHAT Lite hospitals, which can provide initial stabilisation before referring patients to higher-level facilities.Hospitals empanelled under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY will be deemed eligible for designation. Other hospitals can also join, provided they meet the prescribed infrastructure and clinical requirements. These include round-the-clock emergency services, an equipped ICU, emergency operation theatre, imaging facilities, blood storage and ambulance services.The guidelines also prioritise hospitals located near accident-prone stretches, including national and state highways, identified road accident hotspots and municipal roads.The scheme was launched by the Prime Minister on February 13, 2026, with the objective of removing financial barriers to emergency treatment and strengthening trauma care across the country.
Article Summary: The PM-RAHAT (Prime Minister’s Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment) scheme provides cashless treatment of up to Rs 1.5 lakh per accident victim. Non-designated hospitals can provide stabilisation treatment to victims, ensuring that emergency care is not delayed.

Where any fact is not known or not recorded, the answer shall say so expressly and identify the person or record from whom or from which it could be ascertained."Among the 48 questions posed in the interrogatory, which was accompanied by an affidavit from Rahul are: "Whether particular decisions were taken by the commission acting as a body; when and in what manner they were taken; who authorised particular actions in the name of the commission; and how ECINET has been designed, altered and operated."Rahul said the petitioners had no means of access to those facts except through CEC, ECs and DG (IT)."Interrogatories are specifically sought so as to narrow the controversy; obviate the need for oral evidence on matters that are not genuinely in dispute; and to enable the SC to identify, with precision, the matters on which the production of records or further evidence is required," the members said. "Every interrogatory in... is anchored either to a specific averment in the counter affidavit or the supplementary affidavit or a pleading in the writ petition, and is confined to matters of fact. None is in the nature of a roving or fishing inquiry," they added.
Article Summary: Interrogatory procedure is a tool under Civil Procedure Code to seek clarity on assertions of the opposite party. The questions concern decisions related to SIR, EC's claim of unanimity among them, and the change in Form 6. The INDIA bloc invoked the procedure in a writ petition filed under Article 32.

Article Title: Theatre commands are operational imperative, will be implemented soon: CDS; says Agnipath reforms not rollback

NEW DELHI: Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General NS Raja Subramani on Monday said the creation of Integrated Theatre Commands (ITCs) is an “operational imperative” rather than an administrative requirement and that all three services are on the same page and that the country will soon see its rollout. The CDS also noted that the revision to the Agnipath scheme does not mean a “rollback” and its critics are “trying to confuse” the public.Speaking at the ANI National Security Summit, General Subramani explained why integrated command structures are indispensable for future conflicts as such warfare goes beyond traditional boundaries. “Operation Sindoor has aptly proved that multi-domain operations are the need of the hour,” he said.IAF chief Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who accompanied the CDS at the summit, also vouched for theatre commands and dispelled perceptions of institutional resistance by describing air power as “the glue” that will bind jointness, integration, and theatreisation together.Gen Subramani said, “We are not only going to fight on land, air and sea, but also sub-sea, cyber, electronic warfare, spectrum, space spectrum as well as the cognitive spectrum."Clearing the doubts about the Agnipath scheme reforms, Gen Subramani said, “When we started the Agnipath scheme four years ago, it was already decided that the scheme would be reviewed from time to time, keeping in mind its efficacy. Patthar ki lakeer nahi hai (not a line carved in stone), only stupid people do it like that and people who don't want to change it do it like that. He said space has already become a key enabler of modern warfare and stressed the need for India to strengthen its capabilities in satellite-based intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, communication and precision navigation.

Article Title: Covert Cafe: NCB busts secret basement Meow Meow lab in Ahmedabad
Article Text:
"Meow Meow" aka Mephedrone lab tucked away in the basement of a cafe

.

NEW DELHI: What at first glance seemed like a popular local cafe in Ahmedabad's Sarkhej area concealed a clandestine "Meow Meow" aka Mephedrone lab tucked away in its basement. Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has dismantled a clandestine mephedrone manufacturing laboratory whose entrance was cleverly disguised from inside the house behind what appeared to be an almirah and a removable section of tiled flooring.The NCB arrested the owner, Mudasar Ahmed Khan, and seized crores worth drugs in both liquid and powder form. The joint operation was carried out on Sunday with Gujarat Police. During the raid, officials recovered 25 different chemicals weighing 130 kg including methylamine, bromine, and hydrobromic acid. Complete laboratory apparatus, such as heating mantles, digital magnetic stirrers, round-bottom flasks, and separating funnels, was also confiscated.The arrested resident, Mudasar Ahmed Khan, lived at the premises with his family and ran the cafe which served as a delivery point for the contraband, the NCB said. During interrogation, Khan admitted to learning the synthesis process using DIY techniques on YouTube and websites."He procured the raw materials and equipment from suppliers in Mandsaur and Ahmedabad and through online e-commerce platforms. Background checks revealed that Khan has four prior criminal cases registered against him, including charges of attempted murder, rioting, criminal intimidation, and mischief by fire.The agency noted that this bust reflects a wider trend of synthetic drug laboratories operating out of residential spaces, farms, and industrial units across India, following similar recent seizures in Greater Noida, Jewar, and Prayagraj."While the government notified 2-bromo-4-methylpropiophenone as a controlled substance in March 2026 to curb mephedrone production, traffickers are increasingly adopting alternative synthesis methods to bypass regulations," the NCB said.The threat therefore requires continuous intelligence development, close monitoring of precursor supply chains and rapid sharing of information among enforcement agencies, regulators and industry, officials said. The NCB has urged chemical manufacturers and traders to strictly enforce KYC norms and report suspicious bulk orders. Local police have also been instructed to monitor unusual chemical odours and abnormal power usage, while citizens are encouraged to report suspicious activities confidentially via the toll-free Manas helpline at 1933.
Article Summary: "Meow Meow" aka Mephedrone lab tucked away in the basement of a cafe in Ahmedabad. The NCB arrested the owner, Mudasar Ahmed Khan, and seized crores worth drugs. During the raid, officials recovered 25 different chemicals weighing 130 kg.

Article Title: Census 2027: Self-enumeration begins in four states, house-to-house count from December 1
Article Text:
The Census 2027 self-enumeration process has commenced in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa, and Uttarakhand, running until November 30.

NEW DELHI: Self-enumeration for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 began on Monday across Uttar Pradesh , Punjab, Goa and non snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. It will run till Nov 30, followed immediately by house-to-house enumeration starting Dec 1.Population enumeration — which follows completion of houselisting operations across all 35 states/UTs, barring Manipur — shall collect household and individual data across 40 fields, including caste of the respondent. The question relating to the caste is open-ended and the reply will be recorded as declared by the respondent. No documentary proof or verification of one’s caste is required.A notification issued by the home ministry on Sept 5 had advanced the population enumeration phase of ongoing census in the four states in view of the assembly polls there early next year. It is scheduled to run from December 1 to January 4, 2027, preceded by a self-enumeration window from November 16 to 30. A revisional round will be undertaken between Jan 5 and 9 next year.Though Manipur is also due for assembly polls along with the above four states, the census exercise there has been postponed until further notice in view of demands that the national register of citizens (NRC) exercise be undertaken first in the state.Both phases of Census are already complete in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of J&K, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh.In the remaining states and Union territories, population enumeration will be conducted from Jan 25 to Feb 28, 2027 followed by a revisional round from Mar 1 to 5, 2027. The provision for self-enumeration in these states/UTs will be available from Jan 10 to 24, 2027, prior to the commencement of house-to-house visits by enumerators. The reference date for Census in these States/UTs will be 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027.Houselisting operations, which comprise Phase I of Census 2027, have been across all 35 states and Union Territories, except Manipur.For the first time, Census 2027 is being conducted using digital tools, with self-enumeration introduced as an additional facility. It is a secure, convenient and user-friendly web-based facility available in 16 Indian languages.While self-enumeration allows residents to provide their details online at their convenience, enumerators will continue to carry out door-to-door visits in all allocated blocks. Households that do not opt for self-enumeration will be covered during the house-to-house visits.All information collected under the Census Act, 1948, shall remain strictly confidential and is used solely for statistical purposes and development planning.
Article Summary: Census 2027 self-enumeration process has commenced in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa, and Uttarakhand. It will run till Nov 30, followed immediately by house-to- house enumeration starting Dec 1.Population enumeration follows completion of houselisting operations across all 35 states/UTs, barring Manipur.

Article Title: 'No one excluded': CM Yogi Adityanath says Census 2027 will ensure welfare benefits for all

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday said Census 2027 would help identify people excluded from government welfare schemes due to gaps in previous enumeration exercises.Citing the Musahar community in eastern Uttar Pradesh, he said accurate census data was essential to ensure that no eligible person was denied government benefits.Speaking at the launch of the self-enumeration process for Census 2027 in Lucknow, Adityanath said a large section of society remained deprived of welfare schemes because it was overlooked during earlier censuses. He said the data collected during the exercise was later used to formulate government programmes."Through my public engagement, I have observed that a large segment of society remains deprived of government schemes because they were overlooked during the census exercise. Since the very same data is later used to formulate these schemes, this group naturally remains deprived, especially the Musahar community," he said.The chief minister described the Musahar community as one of the most destitute sections of society. He said its members did not even have legal ownership of the land on which their huts stood."Had they been honestly included in past censuses and their extreme distress discussed, then would this community still be on the brink of starvation, even after 70 years of Independence? This raises a serious question about the lack of sensitivity within our entire system," Adityanath said.He said proper documentation of the community's condition could have helped its members gain recognition as beneficiaries of government schemes much earlier."Had we gathered correct information and drawn the government's attention towards their plight, they would have been recognised as rightful beneficiaries of state schemes, and action plans could have been formulated for them in the first Five-Year Plan," he said.Highlighting the importance of accurate population data, Adityanath said the census would help determine the actual requirements for schools, health centres, roads and other basic infrastructure.The chief minister said most development schemes in Uttar Pradesh had so far been based on data from the 2011 Census, making updated demographic information essential for future planning.He also highlighted Uttar Pradesh's demographic significance, saying one in every six people in India lived in the state, while one in every 36 people in the world resided there.Adityanath urged officials and staff involved in the census exercise to perform their duties with integrity, sensitivity and politeness.The exercise will cover Uttar Pradesh's 18 divisions, 75 districts, 350 tehsils, 825 development blocks, 57,694 gram panchayats and 1,04,004 revenue villages. A helpline number, 1855, has also been set up to assist people, he said.Census 2027 will be India's first digital census. Citizens will be able to provide their details from their homes through the dedicated portal.This will be followed by door-to-door enumeration from December 1 to January 4, during which census officials will collect household and individual information.
Article Summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said Census 2027 would help identify people excluded from government welfare schemes. The exercise will involve self-enumeration, allowing citizens to submit details about their households.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites
